name: Claudius Lysias
overview: Claudius Lysias, identified as the chief captain in the book of Acts, was a Roman military officer who intervened during a violent uproar against the Apostle Paul in Jerusalem. When the crowd sought to kill Paul, Lysias quickly took soldiers and centurions to stop the assault, binding Paul with chains and ordering him into custody to investigate the cause of the disturbance. This account highlights Lysias' role in maintaining order and ultimately sending Paul to the governor Felix, demonstrating God's providential protection over Paul as he fulfilled his mission.
